value.hook: Open before adding a 'recovered'/'ready' signal, in-memory dedupe or edge state, a daemon wait bound, or a paused-clock test that does real store IO
value.title: Readiness signals, restart-proof edge state, and test traps from #275/#277 reviews

sections.name: body
sections.value:
- "Ready" must be POSITIVE evidence from the daemon (a returned claim, even an empty page), never our own client timeout (a late 401 looks the same) and never a bare re-register (a daemon that registers but refuses every claim then flaps the banner each retry; store.test `bounded backoff` catches it). Daemon native claims now answer empty at NATIVE_IDLE_ANSWER (55 s) < extension 65 s.
- Edge/dedupe state kept in memory must survive a restart (rebuild once from the last spine event per seat, OnceCell on every path that reads it) and a bounded dedupe must never suppress an UNSEEN key: evict oldest + count it (ping).
- Reviewers (ocelot/calm-badger) check "no launch" claims literally: TmuxPort::list_panes forks when the control client is in backoff; use list_panes_without_launch. A tokio timeout can't preempt a sync-blocking read (control.query_live blocks up to 3 s): run it via spawn_blocking + Handle::block_on and abandon at the deadline.
- Mutations: a guard enforced in two places (pre-check AND select arm) needs both removed or the mutation falsely "survives".
- Paused tokio time + real SQLite/HTTP is fragile (sqlx pool-acquire and reqwest timeouts run on the virtual clock): make the bound a per-service value with a #[cfg(test)] setter and test in real time.
- Tests that pin "a refusal writes nothing" break when you add an audit event: filter exactly that kind; keep "invalid evidence reaches no registry statement" (don't add registry reads on refusal paths).
- Two PRs both appending the last docs/difficulties.md row always conflict; rebase, `conflict://N` @both, range-diff.
